questions.q: In Databricks' own definition, what is 'agentic data engineering'?
options: A marketing term with no specific technical meaning
Running Spark jobs exclusively on serverless compute
Replacing Unity Catalog with a chatbot interface
The shift from manually hand-coding and monitoring pipelines to using autonomous AI agents that understand enterprise context to author, operate, and troubleshoot data workflows
questions.explain: That's the definition straight from Databricks: a shift in who authors, operates, and troubleshoots pipelines, from fully manual to context-aware autonomous agents.

questions.q: Why can a generic coding agent write flawless Python and still fail at a data engineering task, per this lesson?
options: Generic coding agents cannot write Python at all
Flawless code is always wrong in a data pipeline
Spark does not support any AI-generated code
It may not know which upstream definition of a business term (like 'revenue') is the canonical one, since it lacks access to lineage and governance context
questions.explain: The code can be syntactically perfect and still use the wrong upstream table or column because the agent has no visibility into lineage, governance, or which definition is canonical.

questions.q: Which three areas does Lakeflow now cover across the full data lifecycle?
options: Billing, security, and networking
Only batch processing, since Lakeflow does not support streaming
Only ingestion and transformation, with orchestration handled by a separate product
Unified data engineering, agentic development, and autonomous operations
questions.explain: Lakeflow spans unified data engineering (ingestion/transformation on one foundation), agentic development (AI-assisted authoring), and autonomous operations (AI-assisted monitoring and fixes).

questions.q: Why must an AI agent operate on a unified, governed foundation rather than as a standalone external tool, per this lesson?
options: Agents can't function safely in a vacuum — they need complete end-to-end context (lineage, governance policies) to act safely, securely, and accurately
Agents require a graphical user interface to function at all
Unity Catalog cannot be accessed by any external software under any circumstances
Standalone tools are always cheaper to run
questions.explain: Databricks is explicit that agents require complete context to ensure safety, security, and accuracy — context that only exists when the agent runs on the same governed platform as the data.

questions.q: Which problem does this lesson name as being solved specifically by new real-time execution capabilities, rather than by agentic authoring or operations?
options: Tool sprawl across multiple ETL vendors
Dual-engine complexity, where ultra-low-latency streaming previously forced teams to run a second specialized engine like Apache Flink alongside their batch engine
Blind, cron-based orchestration that guesses at data readiness
The 50%+ of time data teams spend fighting fires
questions.explain: Dual-engine complexity for real-time data is specifically what Real-Time Mode for Spark Declarative Pipelines (covered later in this chapter) addresses, eliminating the need for a separate engine like Flink.
